original_question: Determine whether there exists a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G, r), the largest guaranteed Haar measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of G, is strictly less than 1/r^2. In particular, compute the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2).
target_in_paper: Section 5, Question 5.4, in the discussion of the invariant ms for compact topological groups: whether there exists a connected compact group G and a finite number of colors r with ms(G,r)<1/r^2, and specifically what ms(SO(3),2) is. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct open problem: it uses the right invariant ms(G,r), the right threshold 1/r^2, the right ambient class (connected compact groups), and the paper’s singled-out special case SO(3) with r=2. In substance, it is already very close to Question 5.4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
missing_details: The paper works with a compact topological group G equipped with its normalized Haar probability measure μ, not merely an abstract compact group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

A measurable r-coloring means a coloring by finitely many colors whose color classes are measurable subsets of G; equivalently, a measurable partition G=C1∪⋯∪Cr with r∈N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
The group-theoretic notion of symmetry used by the paper is: a subset A⊂G is symmetric if A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

ms(G,r) is defined as a least upper bound (supremum) of ε such that every measurable r-coloring contains a measurable monochromatic symmetric subset A with μ(A)≥ε; attainment is not assumed a priori. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the special case should be stated as the compact connected Lie group SO(3), without broadening to other noncompact or merely locally compact groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
refined_question: Let G be a connected compact topological group with normalized Haar probability measure μ. For r∈N, let ms(G,r) be the supremum of all ε such that every measurable r-coloring G=C1∪⋯∪Cr contains a measurable monochromatic subset A⊂Ci that is symmetric in the group sense, i.e. A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G, and satisfies μ(A)≥ε. Does there exist a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G,r)<1/r^2? In particular, what is the exact value of ms(SO(3),2)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
justification: This is the paper’s official formulation in Section 5: after defining ms(G,r) for compact topological groups via Haar probability measure and measurable colorings, and after recalling the group-theoretic notion of a symmetric subset, the paper asks in Question 5.4 whether the bound 1/r^2 can fail for some connected compact group, and singles out the computation of ms(SO(3),2). The nearby context is exactly Theorems 5.1, 5.2, and 5.3, which give the relevant lower-bound background before the open question is posed. The rewrite therefore stays at the paper’s exact scope and only makes the implicit definitions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
